taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from PA G2 | Inflammation & Healing.

words.clue: Protective vascular and cellular response to injury or infection aimed at eliminating the cause and initiating repair.
Widening of blood vessels that increases blood flow, causing redness and warmth at the injury site.
Protein-rich fluid that accumulates in tissues as a result of increased vascular permeability.
Chemical mediator released from mast cells that causes vasodilation and increased vascular permeability.
The predominant white blood cells that accumulate during the first 6-24 hours of acute inflammation.
Mononuclear leucocytes that become the dominant inflammatory cell type after 24-48 hours.
The movement of white blood cells toward the periphery of blood vessels during inflammatory stasis.
Protein-poor fluid that accumulates due to hydrostatic or oncotic imbalance, not due to active inflammation.
Slowing of blood flow that occurs as fluid leaves the vessel during the inflammatory response.
Latin term for redness, the first cardinal sign of acute inflammation described by Celsus and Virchow.
Latin term for pain, one of the cardinal signs caused by bradykinin and prostaglandins.
Latin term for heat, one of the cardinal signs caused by increased blood flow and metabolic activity.
